reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the general principle that atomic size mismatch enhances glass-forming ability by disrupting crystallization, but none of the cited passages provide specific prior evidence for the effect of Zr substitution in this or any similar high-entropy alloy system. The remaining evidence (E2-E10) only characterizes the baseline alloy's behavior and does not address the proposed intervention.
premises: Adding Zr increases atomic size mismatch and local lattice strain in the alloy.
Increased atomic size mismatch disrupts regular atomic packing and raises the crystallization barrier.
A higher crystallization barrier improves amorphous retention during rapid quenching.
A higher crystallization barrier enhances thermal stability by raising the crystallization onset temperature during reheating.
The proposed substitution of ~2 at% Mn with Zr is sufficient to produce these effects in the Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy.
